plan.topic: Still full the morning after a big holiday meal on tirzepatide: what the label says about slower stomach emptying, and gentle next-day habits
plan.angle: Keep the angle, but replace 'Don't skip or move your injection around the holiday' with: 'Keep to your usual schedule, and ask your prescriber before changing anything.' Keep the label wording without 'so' or 'that's why', for example: 'The label says tirzepatide delays stomach emptying, and that effect is largest after the first dose and diminishes over time.' Then: 'Feeling full after a big meal can have more than one cause.' Keep the untagged gentle tips (eat when hunger returns, no making up for the meal, small portions of leftovers, sip fluids unless you've been told to limit fluids). Keep the emergency card and the don't-stop line word for word, then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Optionally swap the hook to 'big holiday dinner' so it works in every market.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide: Still Full the Morning After Thanksgiving? #shorts
plan.target_keyword: still full next day on mounjaro
plan.why: The holiday-table theme has momentum 90 and peaks Nov 24–27. Full-fast, heartburn and drinks are already done, so this next-morning angle is fresh. It feeds the Thanksgiving long video. | fact-check: Timely, kind and on-pillar. The label wording on gastric emptying (delays it; the effect is largest after the first dose and diminishes over time) is safe as long as it isn't used as the cause of someone's fullness. That matters more here, because for long-term users the label says the effect diminishes. The severe-stomach-pain emergency line and the line for people with diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea are correct to include. One problem: 'Don't skip or move your injection around the holiday' is scheduling advice. It also contradicts the US label, which allows changing the weekly injection day if doses are at least 3 days (72 hours) apart. Replace it with a neutral defer-to-prescriber line. Also: Thanksgiving is a US holiday, so keep the tips general enough for UK/CA/AU viewers, and keep no dates in the narration.

script.cta: No subscribe line and no "link in the description". The script closes with the spoken line "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.", shown on screen as one card ending in a full stop, then the loop line "Remember:", which runs back into sentence 1. Word count: 120 spoken words, recounted scene by scene (14+20+26+13+16+23... see note), inside the tight arm of 90–120. Note: the fact-checker's S3-3 wording adds 2 words, not 1, which would have made 121. To stay at 120, S3-4's first sentence was trimmed from "Keep leftover portions small." to "Small leftover portions.", which matches the list card. Post notes (Exp G): the target long video for the related-video link is Thanksgiving (food/holiday). Captions: build them from the on_screen_text fields. S3-2 stays label wording only, using "diminishes", not "fades", and never adds "so" or "that's why". The safety card is one card.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe. The only factual claim is the S3-2 label line, and it matches section 12.2 of both US labels word for word: "Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying. The delay is largest after the first dose and this effect diminishes over time." Both labels are dated 8/2026, which matches the 28 Aug (Zepbound) and 27 Aug 2026 (Mounjaro) dates on the source list. The keyword names Mounjaro, so citing Mounjaro's own label is correct. Neither label line is used as a cause: there's no "so" and no "that's why". All the required safety lines are there and copied exactly: the severe stomach pain emergency line with "with or without vomiting" and "right away", the scoped don't-stop line, "unless you've been told to limit fluids", and the "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." card. There's no subscribe line and no "link in the description" line. I counted 119 spoken words, inside the tight arm. Our own tips carry no source tags. The four minor fixes below keep the script at 120 words or fewer.

issues.problem: The hook pattern says scene 1's on-screen text matches sentence 1, but the card leaves out the answer, "more than one cause". Muted viewers get the question without the result.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Next-morning fullness on tirzepatide: more than one cause"

issues.claim: Go easy on yourself: big meals can leave anyone full.
issues.problem: This is the second cause that pays off the hook, but it isn't clearly linked to the label line. The retention note ("raises the question of what else is going on") could also push the captions toward suggesting the drug isn't involved. The label says the delay diminishes, not that it stops. Adding "too" presents both causes together.
issues.fix: Narration: "Go easy on yourself: a big meal can leave anyone full, too. When you're ready, start light. No skipping meals to make up for the feast." (+1 word, total 120). Keep on_screen_text: "Start light. No skipping meals to make up."

issues.problem: Telling someone who still feels full to eat straight away could push a person with nausea to eat before they're ready. "When you're ready" keeps the anti-compensation message without that nudge.
issues.fix: Covered by the S3-3 fix above: "When you're ready, start light."

issues.claim: Tirzepatide's stomach-emptying delay: largest after first dose, fades over time
issues.problem: "Fades" is a different verb from the label's "diminishes" and could be read as "goes away". Use the source's own verb.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Tirzepatide's stomach-emptying delay: largest after first dose, diminishes over time"
